subject.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads

question: What persistent-state recovery contract should doctor use when a legacy plugin source exceeds the safety cap: retain it untouched with a clear warning, or implement a bounded migration/recovery mechanism before archival?
rationale: The current code converts an oversized persistent source into an unrecognized archive without importing its state, and the acceptable recovery guarantee is an upgrade/data-contract decision rather than a safe blind mechanical choice.

options.title: Retain oversized sources and warn
options.body: Leave the legacy source at its recognized path, emit a clear doctor warning, and avoid claiming migration until a recovery path exists.

options.title: Add bounded recovery before archival
options.body: Implement and validate a memory-bounded parser or explicit export/recovery flow that preserves the data before any archival rename.

recommendation.title: Retain oversized sources and warn
recommendation.body: Leave the legacy source at its recognized path, emit a clear doctor warning, and avoid claiming migration until a recovery path exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest branch commit introduced the archival behavior requiring a recovery-contract decision.
